value.content: 11-03-2025 Information About Brokerage Services Texas law requires all real estate license holders to give the following informa(cid:415)on about brokerage services to prospec(cid:415)ve buyers, tenants, sellers and landlords. TYPES OF REAL ESTATE LICENSE HOLDERS: · A BROKER is responsible for all brokerage ac(cid:415)vi(cid:415)es, including acts performed by sales agents sponsored by the broker. · A SALES AGENT must be sponsored by a broker and works with clients on behalf of the broker. A BROKER’S MINIMUM DUTIES REQUIRED BY LAW (A client is the person or party that the broker represents): · Put the interests of the client above all others, including the broker’s own interests; · Inform the client of any material informa(cid:415)on about the property or transac(cid:415)on received by the broker; · Answer the client’s ques(cid:415)ons and present any offer to or counter-offer from the client; and · Treat all par(cid:415)es to a real estate transac(cid:415)on honestly and fairly. WRITTEN AGREEMENTS ARE REQUIRED IN CERTAIN SITUATIONS: A license holder who performs brokerage ac(cid:415)vity for a prospec(cid:415)ve buyer of residen(cid:415)al property must enter into a wri(cid:425)en agreement with the buyer before showing any residen(cid:415)al property to the buyer or if no residen(cid:415)al property will be shown, before presen(cid:415)ng an offer on behalf of the buyer. This wri(cid:425)en agreement must contain specific informa(cid:415)on required by Texas law. For more informa(cid:415)on on these requirements, see sec(cid:415)on 1101.563 of the Texas Occupa(cid:415)ons Code. Even if a wri(cid:425)en agreement is not required, to avoid disputes, all agreements between you and a broker should be in wri(cid:415)ng and clearly establish: (i) the broker’s du(cid:415)es and responsibili(cid:415)es to you and your obliga(cid:415)ons under the agreement; and (ii) the amount or rate of compensa(cid:415)on the broker will receive and how this amount is determined. A LICENSE HOLDER CAN REPRESENT A PARTY IN A REAL ESTATE TRANSACTION: AS AGENT FOR OWNER (SELLER/LANDLORD): The broker becomes the property owner's agent through an agreement with the owner, usually in a wri(cid:425)en lis(cid:415)ng to sell or property management agreement. An owner's agent must perform the broker’s minimum du(cid:415)es above and must inform the owner of any material informa(cid:415)on about the property or transac(cid:415)on known by the agent, including informa(cid:415)on disclosed to the agent by the buyer or buyer’s agent. An owner’s agent fees are not set by law and are fully nego(cid:415)able. AS AGENT FOR BUYER/TENANT: The broker becomes the buyer/tenant's agent by agreeing to represent the buyer, usually through a wri(cid:425)en representa(cid:415)on agreement. A buyer's agent must perform the broker’s minimum du(cid:415)es above and must inform the buyer of any material informa(cid:415)on about the property or transac(cid:415)on known by the agent, including informa(cid:415)on disclosed to the agent by the seller or seller’s agent. A buyer/tenant’s agent fees are not set by law and are fully nego(cid:415)able. AS AGENT FOR BOTH - INTERMEDIARY: To act as an intermediary between the par(cid:415)es the broker must first obtain the wri(cid:425)en agreement of each party to the transac(cid:415)on. The wri(cid:425)en agreement must state who will pay the broker and, in conspicuous bold or underlined print, set forth the broker's obliga(cid:415)ons as an intermediary. A broker who acts as an intermediary: · Must treat all par(cid:415)es to the transac(cid:415)on impar(cid:415)ally and fairly; · May, with the par(cid:415)es' wri(cid:425)en consent, appoint a different license holder associated with the broker to each party (owner and buyer) to communicate with, provide opinions and advice to, and carry out the instruc(cid:415)ons of each party to the transac(cid:415)on. · Must not, unless specifically authorized in wri(cid:415)ng to do so by the party, disclose: ᴑ that the owner will accept a price less than the wri(cid:425)en asking price; ᴑ that the buyer/tenant will pay a price greater than the price submi(cid:425)ed in a wri(cid:425)en offer; and ᴑ any confiden(cid:415)al informa(cid:415)on or any other informa(cid:415)on that a party specifically instructs the broker in wri(cid:415)ng not to disclose, unless required to do so by law. A LICENSE HOLDER CAN SHOW PROPERTY TO A BUYER/TENANT WITHOUT REPRESENTING THE BUYER/TENANT IF: · The broker has not agreed with the buyer/tenant, either orally or in wri(cid:415)ng, to represent the buyer/tenant; · The broker is not otherwise ac(cid:415)ng as the buyer/tenant’s agent at the (cid:415)me of showing the property; · The broker does not provide the buyer/tenant opinions or advice regarding the property or real estate transac(cid:415)ons generally; and · The broker does not perform any other act of real estate brokerage for the buyer/tenant. Before showing a residen(cid:415)al property to an unrepresented prospec(cid:415)ve buyer, a license holder must enter into a wri(cid:425)en agreement that contains the informa(cid:415)on required by sec(cid:415)on 1101.563 of the Texas Occupa(cid:415)ons Code. The agreement may not be exclusive and must be limited to no more than 14 days. LICENSE HOLDER CONTACT INFORMATION: This no(cid:415)ce is being provided for informa(cid:415)on purposes. It does not create an obliga(cid:415)on for you to use the broker’s services. Please acknowledge receipt of this no(cid:415)ce below and retain a copy for your records.
